meta.title: Surface-code memory below threshold

paper.title: Quantum error correction below the surface code threshold

meta.summary: A distance-3, 5 and 7 rotated surface-code memory on the 105-qubit Willow processor, with a 1.1 µs error-correction cycle and real-time decoding.
meta.program: The compiler's own surface-code declaration and an encoded program of R rounds of `extract`, then a `decode`. The compiler's back end lowers it to physical gates, resets, routes, measurements and decodes.
meta.twin: The distance-7 patch of the paper's square grid: 49 data and 48 measure transmons, a tunable coupler between every diagonal pair, 25 ns XY rotations and 42 ns CZ from the paper, 500 ns readout and 160 ns reset from the group's 2023 paper. The control system is QuantumOS's RISC-Q model, the decoder Helios union-find compiled for its cores.
findings: Every operation of the listing ran inside its listed window on the twin at d = 3, 5 and 7.

On the same gate durations, the compiler's surface-code round takes 2.5 to 4.0 µs where the paper's cycle is 1.1 µs: the compiler's round runs at most (d² − 1)/2 gates at once, while the device runs every check in parallel (four CZ layers, two H, measure and reset come to about 0.95 µs).

The decoder compiled for RISC-Q's 500 MHz RISC-V core, timed by the core model that matches its RTL cycle for cycle, is slower than the paper's software decoder at d = 5 (191 µs for 10 rounds against 63 µs): a property of the decoder's placement, not of the system call.
limits: The data qubits are not read out at the end: the compiler's encoded level has no transversal data readout in this form.
Helios's decoding graph holds d rounds; a longer decode runs in consecutive windows without overlap.
Qubit frequencies and pulse shapes are not published; the twin uses RISC-Q's pulse shapes with the paper's durations. 8 of the 105 qubits (leakage removal) are not placed.

device.title: Google 105-qubit processor (Willow), distance-7 patch
device.basis: Durations of gates from the paper; readout and reset from the group's 2023 paper. Geometry: the distance-7 patch on the square grid. Frequencies, pulse shapes and readout multiplexing are not published; the chip reuses RISC-Q's x6y3 pulse shapes with these durations. The control electronics are QuantumOS's RISC-Q model, not Google's.

readoutNs.source: Google Quantum AI, Nature 614, 676 (2023), arXiv:2207.06431, Fig. 1 (the 2025 paper gives no readout duration)

resetNs.source: Google Quantum AI, arXiv:2207.06431, Fig. 1 (the 2025 paper gives no reset duration)
